t.6.72.2: Then Rāma, conqueror of enemy cities, summoning up his fortitude, spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa, who was seated near him, in the presence of the monkeys.
t.6.72.1: Hearing those words of his, Rāghava, worn down by grief, could not clearly grasp what had been said by that rākṣasa.
t.6.72.3: O Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the Nairṛtas, I wish to hear once more the words that were spoken by you; tell me what you intend to say.
t.6.72.4: Having heard Rāghava's words, Vibhīṣaṇa, skilled in speech, once again spoke these words concerning that matter.
t.6.72.5: O mighty-armed one, the posting of troops that you commanded has been carried out just so, O hero, immediately upon your word.
t.6.72.6: All those divisions of the army were distributed on every side, and the troop-leaders too were stationed in their proper places, each according to his allotted share.
t.6.72.7: But there is something more I must make known to you; hear it, O greatly renowned one. When you are tormented without cause, we too are tormented at heart.
t.6.72.8: Cast off this grief, O king, this anguish that has come upon you falsely; therefore let this anxiety, which only swells the joy of your enemies, be abandoned.
t.6.72.9: Let effort be made, O hero, and let cheerfulness be embraced, if Sītā is to be won by you and the night-rangers are to be slain.
t.6.72.10: O Raghunandana, I shall speak; let my beneficial words be heard. It is well that this Saumitri go, surrounded by a great army, and, reaching Nikumbhilā, slay Rāvaṇi in battle.
t.6.72.12: Through his austerity and by the granting of a boon from Svayambhū, that hero obtained the Brahmaśiras weapon and horses that go wherever they wish.
t.6.72.11: The great archer, victorious in battle, was intent on slaying Rāvaṇi with arrows loosed from the circle of his bow, arrows like the venom of poisonous serpents.
t.6.72.13: "O foe of Indra, the enemy who slays you, the aggressor, before you have reached Nikumbhilā and before you have offered oblations into the fire, he shall be your death." Thus, O king, was the death of that wise one ordained.
t.6.72.14: O Rāma, direct that mighty one to the slaying of Indrajit; when he is slain, know that Rāvaṇa is slain along with his friends and kin.
t.6.72.16: For he, the knower of the Brahmāstra, wise, possessed of great magic and great strength, renders senseless in battle even the gods together with Varuṇa.
t.6.72.15: Having heard Vibhīṣaṇa's words, Rāma then spoke: "I know the illusory power of that fierce one, O you of true valour."
t.6.72.18: But Rāghava, having understood the power of illusion wielded by his evil-minded foe, spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa, who was endowed with renown.
t.6.72.17: O illustrious hero, the course of him who moves through the sky, standing in his chariot, cannot be discerned, just like that of the sun when it is shrouded in a mass of clouds.
t.6.72.20: Surrounded by the army together with Jāmbava, the lord of the bears, slay that son of the rākṣasa, who is skilled in the power of illusion.
t.6.72.19: O Lakṣmaṇa, surrounded by all of that army which belongs to the lord of the monkeys, and together with the troop leaders headed by Hanumān...
t.6.72.21: This great-souled night-ranger, together with his ministers, who knows that place well, will follow behind you.
t.6.72.22: Having heard the words of Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa of fearsome prowess, accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa, took up another excellent bow.
t.6.72.23: Armed and armored, bearing a sword, arrows, and a golden bow, Saumitri touched the feet of Rāma and, filled with joy, spoke.
t.6.72.24: Today the arrows springing forth from my bow, having pierced Rāvaṇi, will descend upon Laṅkā like swans alighting on a lotus pond.
t.6.72.25: This very day my arrows, loosed from the string of my mighty bow, will slay him and scatter the body of that fierce one.
t.6.72.26: Having spoken these words thus before his brother, the radiant Lakṣmaṇa, eager for the slaying of Rāvaṇi, went forth in haste.
t.6.72.28: The valiant prince Lakṣmaṇa, accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa, his brother having performed the rites invoking his welfare, departed in haste.
t.6.72.27: Having saluted the feet of his father and walked around him in reverence, he set out for Nikumbhilā, the shrine guarded by Rāvaṇi.
t.6.72.29: Then Hanūmān, surrounded by many thousands of monkeys, and Vibhīṣaṇa together with his ministers followed Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.72.30: Swiftly surrounded by a great army of monkeys, he also saw the host of the king of the bears stationed on the path.
t.6.72.31: Having travelled a long way, Saumitri, the delight of his friends, saw from afar the army of the lord of the rākṣasas drawn up in battle formation.
t.6.72.32: O subduer of foes, having attained mastery of magic, that delight of the Raghus stood bow in hand, according to the rite of Brahman, ready to conquer.
t.6.72.33: He entered that army of his foes as one enters darkness: manifold, gleaming with spotless weapons, dense with banners and vast with great chariots, most terrifying and of immeasurable force.
